sets.title: The decline of the high street
text: Town centres that once thrived are now struggling {{1}} as shopping habits change. The {{2}} of online retail has accelerated this decline.

Shoppers increasingly expect a wide {{3}} of products available instantly, which puts smaller shops under constant pressure. Councils have also become {{4}} on business rates that are shrinking year on year.
Several cities have invested heavily in {{5}} projects to attract new businesses, although not every scheme has {{6}} reversed the trend. Local {{7}} support schemes have had mixed results.
The long-term future of many high streets remains a matter of considerable {{8}}.

questions.explanation: The adverb 'economically' describes the manner in which the centres are struggling.
The noun 'growth' is needed after 'the' and before 'of online retail'.
The noun 'variety' fits after 'a wide' and before 'of products'.
The adjective 'reliant' is needed after 'become' and before 'on'.
The noun 'regeneration' is needed to describe the type of projects.
The adverb 'successfully' describes how the scheme has, or has not, reversed the trend.
The adjective 'financial' describes the type of support schemes.
The negative noun 'uncertainty' fits after 'considerable', showing the future is unclear.
